verdicts.note: Scènes écossaises, Op. 138 is an OBOE work: IMSLP gives 'oboe, orchestra' (1892; Hamelle, Paris, 1893, plates J. 3595-97 H; dedicated to Georges Gillet), 3 pieces (Légende pastorale, Sérénade à Mabel, Marche des Highlanders), with oboe & piano arrangements (Hamelle 1892) and later oboe (or flute) & piano editions (Southern, Accolade, Ludwig; Kalmus reprints the orchestral material). No violin version is listed on IMSLP or in any publisher listing found; the 'oboe or violin' evidence in the draft is unsupported.

(not flagged verify) Violin Concerto in D minor, Op. 29 is UNPUBLISHED: IMSLP only has a holograph manuscript (n.d., ca. 1870), 'Extra Information: unpublished', and notes that Godard seems not to have orchestrated it himself (orchestration by Martin Yates released on a 2022 Dutton CD). No published edition, so out of scope; the published concertos are Op. 35 (already listed) and Op. 131 (N13).

verdicts.title: Sérénade andalouse, Op. 128 No. 5
verdicts.note: (not flagged verify) IMSLP '6 Morceaux, Op.128' (violin, piano; Leduc, Paris, 1892, plates A.L. 8998-9003) lists the six pieces as: 1 Rêverie, 2 Gavotte, 3 Adagio pathétique, 4 Mazurka sentimentale, 5 Sérénade andalouse, 6 Staccato-valse. So No. 5 is 'Sérénade andalouse', not 'Sérénade'. Siblings N6-N8 and existing id 968 match the IMSLP titles; No. 6 is missing from the queue (see gaps).

(not flagged verify) Exists. IMSLP: original violin & orchestra (Simrock, Berlin, 1893, plates 10012-16; dedicated to Jeanne Bourgand), plus a violin & piano version credited to Godard on IMSLP. Five movements: À l'ombre; Sous la charmille; En regardant le ciel; Danse rustique; La Fée du hallier. The parenthetical '(Suite de cinq morceaux)' in the queued title is optional; 'En plein air, Op. 145' alone is the IMSLP title.

(not flagged verify) Exists as a posthumous salon piece: IMSLP lists it for 'violin or cello or flute, piano' (Paris: Choudens, ca. 1895-96, plate A.C. 10,243; 'Jeunesse, souvenir', Oeuvres posthumes Nos. 9 and 11). Obscure and violin is only one of three allowed solo instruments; keep only if tiny salon pieces are wanted.

(not flagged verify, low confidence) IMSLP's Godard work list gives Op. 119 'Menuet-Pompadour' as a song for voice and piano (text by J.-B. Rousseau), with a violin & piano version noted alongside. The only violin edition found is an unattributed anthology print, Les Perles du Violoniste II,27 (Warsaw: Gebethner & Wolff, plate G2968W, n.d., ed. Maurice Rosen). So it is an obscure transcription of a song, not a documented violin original; keep it out unless you want such prints. If kept, house style would be 'Menuet-Pompadour, Op. 119 (orig. voice)'.

(not flagged verify) Confirmed: violin & piano, Intermezzo / Berceuse / Tarantelle, Berlin: Fürstner, 1883 (plates 2159-61), dedicated to Hubert Léonard. IMSLP's work list also labels it 'Violin Sonata No. 5'. (Op. 116 'Suite de trois morceaux' is a different, flute & piano work.)
(not flagged verify) Confirmed: solo violin, B minor; Prélude, Gavotte, Adagio, Menuet; Durand, Schoenewerk, Paris, plate D.S. et Cie. 2453 (ca. 1877?); dedicated to Léon Reynier.

(not flagged verify) Confirmed and published (posthumously): Paris: Choudens, 1896, plate A.C. 10,165; A minor; Sarabande, Rigodon, Adagio ma non troppo - Moderato, Bourrée; composed c. 1894-5. No opus number (IMSLP lists it as Op. posth.).

gaps.title: Légende et Scherzo, Op. 3
gaps.edition: Paris: G. Flaxland, 1867 (dedicated to Henri Vieuxtemps); reissued Durand, Schoenewerk & Cie., plate D.S. & Cie. 2412 (1878); IMSLP
gaps.note: Two linked movements, Légende (Allegro vivace) and Scherzo (Vivace), both in G major. Listed as a violin & piano work on IMSLP's Godard work list (https://imslp.org/wiki/List_of_works_by_Benjamin_Godard). Level is a guess.

gaps.title: Staccato-valse, Op. 128 No. 6
gaps.edition: Paris: Alphonse Leduc, 1892 (complete score and violin part plate A.L. 9003; IMSLP)
gaps.note: The sixth piece of the set; the queue has Nos. 1, 2, 4, 5 and existing id 968 is No. 3, so No. 6 is the only one missing. Level is a guess (staccato waltz).

gaps.title: Aurore (Berceuse), Op. posth.
gaps.edition: Paris: Choudens, ca. 1895 (Oeuvres posthumes Nos. 1 and 6, plate A.C. 10286; IMSLP)
gaps.note: Low priority, same status as queued N4 'Jeunesse' (posthumous Choudens salon piece; the violin version is the 'berceuse' No. 6, cello version No. 1). IMSLP's work list also names Conte nouveau, Le Désir (Allegro) and Regrets (Andantino) as posthumous violin & piano pieces and Pensée du soir for 2 violins, but none has an IMSLP page/scan, so they are not proposed. The Canzonetta (movement of the Concerto romantique, Schirmer 1894 ed. Mittell) was deliberately left out as an excerpt of an already-listed work.

existing_issues.issue: Title 'Berceuse (from Jocelyn), arr.' has no arranger and no opus number. The Berceuse is from Godard's opera Jocelyn, Op. 100 (Act II, 'Oh! ne t'éveille pas encore'). IMSLP lists violin & piano versions under the headings 'For Violin and Piano (Godard)' (Mainz: Schott, 1895; Leipzig: W. Reissbrodt, n.d.), '(Meyer)' and '(Tobani)'. I could not confirm which of these is the catalogue's version, so the '(arr. Surname)' part needs the owner's choice.
